objects: sigma-algebra definition; finite-union implication; countable-intersection corollary and proof; trivial, powerset, Borel, and reduced-space examples
checks: Derived Omega in calA from empty set plus complement; derived finite unions by padding with empty sets; independently checked the countable-intersection proof via De Morgan. Tested absolute assertion about impossibility of a probability on every subset using an explicit atomic measure.
rejected_hypotheses: Sigma-algebra axioms fail to imply finite unions: rejected; set A1=A, A2=B, Ai=empty for i>=3 and apply countable closure.
Countable-intersection proof is circular: rejected; it uses only complement closure, countable-union closure, and De Morgan.
The finite/countable powerset example is invalid: rejected; arbitrary nonnegative point masses summing to one define a probability on the powerset.
result: one P1 overstatement in Borel example

checks: Verified |product_i Omega_i|=N^10000 when every factor has N=13,983,816 elements. Verified A=union_{i=1}^{9999} Ai exactly describes at least one adjacent match. Checked probability claim against distinct admissible probability laws and, conditionally, the iid-uniform formula 1-(1-1/N)^9999.
rejected_hypotheses: The adjacent-match index range is off by one: rejected; 10000 draws have exactly 9999 adjacent pairs.
The cardinality N^10000 is wrong: rejected under the declared same-size single-draw spaces.
The event union does not allow a match: rejected; membership is equivalent to existence of i with equal consecutive coordinates.

objects: De Morgan exercise; two-envelopes formulation; supplementary solution and all displayed probability equalities; logistic randomized strategy
checks: Verified De Morgan exercise identity pointwise. Derived success probability from the two equiprobable observed-value cases. For a<b, p(x)=1/(1+e^x) is defined on R, lies in (0,1), and is strictly decreasing, so p(a)-p(b)>0; checked negative and arbitrarily large values remain within the stated domain.
rejected_hypotheses: The two-envelopes formula has a sign error: rejected; success is switch after a and retain after b, yielding 1/2 p(a)+1/2(1-p(b)).
The logistic rule fails for negative values: rejected; e^x>0 for every real x, hence p(x) is in (0,1) and remains strictly decreasing.
The claimed advantage is a uniform positive margin: rejected as an interpretation; the final sentence correctly limits the claim to pointwise strict positivity and notes it can be arbitrarily small.
result: no mathematical finding; implicit fair initial choice and independent auxiliary randomization are standard reading of the stated randomized strategy.
